what: Sessions produced by tools/controlled_traffic/generate.py against a throwaway engine on loopback. Labels were assigned by construction: each session carries the label of the scripted scenario that produced it. None of this is traffic from real attackers.

label_definitions.benign: Connects and leaves, mistypes one login, or browses ordinary pages. No attack behaviour.
label_definitions.reconnaissance: Finds out what is there without changing anything: version scans, path enumeration, system enumeration after login.
label_definitions.exploitation: Tries to gain or keep access: password guessing runs, injection and traversal requests, download-and-run, persistence.
label_definitions.exfiltration: Reads sensitive files and sends them to another host.

limits: The scripted shell and web scenarios were written by the team that wrote the rules, so the rule layer is being scored on traffic resembling what it was built for.
Every session comes from one source address on loopback.
A scenario's label is applied to every session inside its window; a scanner's individual probe connections all carry the scan's label.
